rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose choice when exchanging something for a new or equivalent one.

example.english: I need to replace my phone with a new one.
example.traditional: 部手機壞咗，我要換部新嘅。
example.jyutping: bou6 sau2 gei1 waai6 zo2 ngo5 jiu3 wun6 bou6 san1 ge3

rows.note: Use this for putting an object back in its former physical place or position, rather than exchanging it for another one.

example.english: Remember to replace the book on the shelf when you’re done.
example.traditional: 用完本書，記得放返喺書架。
example.jyutping: jung6 jyun4 bun2 syu1 gei3 dak1 fong3 faan1 hai2 syu1 gaa3

rows.note: Use this when one person or thing takes the place of another or is used instead of it.

example.english: Nowadays, many restaurants use electronic menus to replace paper menus.
example.traditional: 而家好多餐廳用電子餐牌代替紙餐牌。
example.jyutping: ji4 gaa1 hou2 do1 caan1 teng1 jung6 din6 zi2 caan1 paai4 doi6 tai3 zi2 caan1 paai4

rows.note: Use this when paying money back or returning money that was borrowed or owed.

example.english: I’ll replace the money I owe you next month when I get paid.
example.traditional: 我下個月出糧就還返啲錢畀你。
example.jyutping: ngo5 haa6 go3 jyut6 ceot1 loeng4 zau6 waan4 faan1 di1 cin2 bei2 nei5
